do_not_copy: Do not import XML/FRBR/IRI vocabulary wholesale.
Do not require ALTO output or infer reading order from XML order.
Do not treat hashes as authenticity or fetch.txt URLs as safe implicit network authority.
Do not expose arbitrary SQL or unrestricted plugin writes over canonical DB.
Do not copy cloud/service topology or make publishing authority implicit.
Do not adopt ELI RDF/URI identity as core.
Do not adopt generic node/edge storage or statement-per-field provenance by default.
Do not make package format the internal database model or auto-fetch arbitrary URLs.
Do not require IIIF server/JSON-LD or assume all capabilities.
Do not assume linked archived pages represent the same historical instant.
Do not turn Notebook bookkeeping into product architecture or source-count theater.
Do not adopt full OCFL object layout/inventory unless export/scale later proves value.
Do not use full universal undo/event history as canonical ActaKit history.
Do not promise external canonical IDs are permanent or auto-merge by name.
Do not import US legislative ontology/categorization wholesale.
Do not copy consumer document-management workflow or tags as ActaKit ontology.
Do not make Popolo the national/domain ontology for ActaKit.
Do not store all runtime events forever.
Do not implement PROV-O/RDF globally or make every operation canonical.
Do not implement ontology-wide RDF/OWL reasoning or hundreds of generated relation properties.
Do not adopt RDF/SHACL runtime for core validation.
Do not impose a national SKOS/RDF taxonomy.
Do not use network/synced filesystem, direct external writes, naive live file copy or FTS as authority.
Do not treat every selection as a new document or require one global metadata template.
Do not import RDF ontology or assume it captures civic accountability.
Do not require WARC for ordinary source adapters.
Do not import RDF/JSON-LD or graph storage as runtime requirements.
Do not atomize ActaKit into Wikidata property/snaks or implement consensus ranks.
Do not expose DB schema as supported write API or embed canonical annotations into source files.
